[[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]]
'''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|en|Saito, Miyazaki|qid=Q850479|lt=Saito, Miyazaki}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|qid=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|qid=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|qid=Q513737|lt=Hyūga Province}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.<ref name="mppf">[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024.</ref>

== name ==
The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}.<ref name="mppf"/> Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."<ref name="神々">From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''.</ref>

== Deities ==
* '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)<ref name="mppf"/><ref>The shrine's official records.</ref>
*: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life.<ref name="mppf"/>
*: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|en|Amazake|qid=Q455990|lt=Amazake}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing.<ref name="mppf"/> A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim.<ref name="mppf"/>

Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto.

== History ==
=== Foundation ===
The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|en|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|qid=Q3469314|lt=Saitobaru Kofun Cluster}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses.<ref name="神々"/>

According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.<ref>''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976.</ref>

Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|en|Motoori Norinaga|qid=Q384647|lt=Motoori Norinaga}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|en|Wajinden|qid=Q1135798|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed.<ref name="神々"/>

=== Historical Overview ===
The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE.

In the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|qid=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship.<ref name="地名"/> Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine.<ref name="地名"/>

The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|en|Itō clan|qid=Q2975280|lt=Itō clan}}.<ref name="地名"/> 

In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine Ranking system.

=== Historical types ===
* 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki'').
* 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'').

* '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto.

[[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]]
'''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|en|Saito, Miyazaki|qid=Q850479|lt=Saito, Miyazaki}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|qid=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|qid=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|qid=Q513737|lt=Hyūga Province}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.<ref name="mppf">[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024.</ref>

== name ==
The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1781862}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}.<ref name="mppf"/> Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."<ref name="神々">From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''.</ref>

== Deities ==
* '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1781862}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)<ref name="mppf"/><ref>The shrine's official records.</ref>
*: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life.<ref name="mppf"/>
*: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|en|Amazake|qid=Q455990|lt=Amazake}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing.<ref name="mppf"/> A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim.<ref name="mppf"/>

Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto.

== History ==
=== Foundation ===
The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1781862}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|en|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|qid=Q3469314|lt=Saitobaru Kofun Cluster}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses.<ref name="神々"/>

According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.<ref>''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976.</ref>

Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|en|Motoori Norinaga|qid=Q384647|lt=Motoori Norinaga}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|en|Wajinden|qid=Q1135798|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed.<ref name="神々"/>

=== Historical Overview ===
The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE.

In the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|qid=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship.<ref name="地名"/> Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine.<ref name="地名"/>

The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|en|Itō clan|qid=Q2975280|lt=Itō clan}}.<ref name="地名"/> 

In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system.

=== Historical types ===
* 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki'').
* 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'').

== Sub-Shrines ==
* '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto.
* '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto.
* '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto.
* '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others.
* '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Natural Monument ===
[[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]]
* '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).<ref>[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets].</ref>
